title: Applied Seller Adjustment
description: Record of one change the seller applied to a live media buy under a seller-held change term (change_terms[] with holder seller). It is the readback in get_media_buys applied_adjustments[] and its adjustment_id is the notification_id of media_buy.allowance_applied. Each application advances the buy's revision and mints an accepted successor proposal, named by accepted_proposal_id, that carries the terms forward. The revision history entry records the origin in actor (seller_system for automation, seller_operator when a person applied it), plus term_id and reason, and the account change feed record carries the same origin.kind, term_id and reason. Experimental in AdCP 3.3 (media_buy.seller_adjustment_allowances).

adjustment_id.description: Seller-assigned identifier, unique within the seller's account namespace (it is the notification_id) and stable across re-emissions.

term_id.description: The seller-held change_terms[] entry in the accepted commercial_terms that authorized this change.

revision.description: The media buy revision this application created.

accepted_proposal_id.description: The accepted successor proposal minted by this application (offer_reason term_applied). Its parent_proposal_id is the proposal that was accepted before, and its base_media_buy_revision is revision minus one. It becomes the buy's accepted_proposal_id.

reason.description: Short machine-readable reason code, such as forecast_shortfall; the same shape as the reason on an account change record. Human-readable text goes in the history entry's summary.

action.description: The term's action: decrease_budget, update_impression_goal, update_flight_dates or update_targeting.

package_id.description: The package the changed purchase maps to, when the seller assigned one.

previous_value.description: The affected field's value before this change: the purchase budget or impressions (a number), an object with start_time and end_time (update_flight_dates), or the purchase targeting_overlay (update_targeting).

value.description: The affected field's value after this change, in the same shape as previous_value.

alternate_index.description: Position in the term's constraints.alternates[] that was used, when the change selected an alternate.

skipped_alternates.description: Earlier alternates that were not used, each with why it was unavailable, so the first-available rule is auditable.

examples.description: A budget release applied within a seller-held decrease_budget term with a 4,000 USD floor
